topic: Antipsychotic physical health monitoring in children and young people
usual_baseline: Baseline bloods vary widely: 92% in one clinic and inpatients, 38% in community. Ongoing monitoring is poor: complete monitoring bloods 33%, full baseline 0%, six-monthly measures 16–20%, waist circumference 0%. Movement disorder assessment 0–54%. Samples are tiny, 7–26 patients.
fix_that_works: A spreadsheet to track antipsychotic prescriptions: blood-test monitoring 17% to 100%, medication information 50% to 67%, but only 3 patients at re-audit [3413].
fix_that_fails: Recording in clinic letters with the schedule at the front of notes changed little: complete bloods 33% to 44%, baseline ECG 75% to 67%, current schedule 42% to 38%, 0% on PARIS [3169]. The unlicensed-indication protocol fell from 13% to 0% [3413].
consultant_advice: Every audit finds the same gaps, in samples too small to show change. Audit who owns the monitoring when bloods and ECGs are sent to GPs, as results are hard to track. Pooling data across teams would give numbers large enough to re-audit.
